html:
A Korean scholar, official and engineer of the late Joseon dynasty, known by his pen name Dasan. He is the leading figure of Silhak, the Practical Learning movement, which turned Confucian study toward real problems of farming, trade and government.

He was a trusted adviser to King Jeongjo. For the new fortress of Hwaseong at Suwon he designed a crane and pulley system, drawing on Western books that had come through China, which cut the building time.

Some of his family were among Korea's first Catholics, and when Jeongjo died in 1800 the court turned on them. His brother was executed in the persecution of 1801, and Jeong was exiled to the far south for eighteen years. There he wrote some 500 volumes, among them guides for honest local officials and plans for land reform and a stronger state. Pardoned in 1818, he lived quietly until his death. His story links the Practical Learning and the arrival of Catholicism in Korea.
